title: The Invisible Crisis: Innovating for the Age of Extreme Heat
description:
Campus Deep Tech, Anywhere Ventures, The Hazelwood Network, and Tailwind Futures are bringing together a curated group of startups, investors, industry leaders, and academics during Climate Week NYC to explore the mounting challenges posed by extreme heat globally and novel technologies being developed to help people and industries adapt.

Discover breakthrough technologies
Engage directly with innovators working at the frontier of extreme heat resilience and cooling technologies
Identify investment and partnership opportunities
Become part of the region's growing deep tech ecosystem

description:
Organized by Kanop, PUR and Removall, the Nature-Based Carbon Forum brings together leading stakeholders from across the carbon market to explore what it will take to scale high-integrity, tree- and forest-based carbon projects.
Through expert discussions and peer exchange, the Forum will examine the latest developments, opportunities and challenges across restoration and conservation - from project integrity and implementation to market demand, finance and long-term impact.
The programme will focus on four key areas:
ARR - REDD+ - Agroforestry - Mangroves

title: Climate Solutions Showcase
description:

From recycleable flood barriers to passive cooling technology, the Trust's Climate Piloting Program supports more than two dozen innovative solutions that are paving the way for more resilient and sustainable cities.
Join us on Wednesday, September 23, to see emerging tech in action, hear the founders pitch, and connect with the dynamic climate piloting ecosystem on Governors Island.
Event Details
12-3PM: Climate Solutions Showcase at LMCC’s Arts Center at Governors Island
Featuring an Adaptation Pitch Hour, fireside chats, live demos, and more
3:15-4PM: Climate Tech Crawl
Outdoor walking tour of Governors Island’s climate innovations
Light bites and refreshments included. Afterwards, join us at Taco Vista for a Climate Trivia Happy Hour with Green Apple Trivia--click here to register.
Featuring:
it’s electric, Behind the Meter Level 2 EV charging solution that brings clean transportation infrastructure and the benefits of the green economy into neighborhoods around the U.S.
KlimaKover, Membrane-assisted radiant cooling shelter, created by Henning Larsen in collaboration with the University of Pennsylvania
Previsico, Surface water flood forecasting technology
Rego, AI-powered waste auditing and analytics platform for the built environment
Sunphade, Adaptive solar control for buildings

title: (pre)NY Climate Week Founder Speed Matching
description:
Looking for a co-founder to build a climate startup with? C2FM's founder speed matching format is going NYC-wide for the first time.
Here's how it works:
You'll apply by answering a few quick questions, and C2FM's founder matching algorithm will decide who you are most compatible with as a co-founder.
You'll go through 10 rounds of 5-minute conversations with founders who could be a real fit.
After each round, you mark yes or no on the people you met.
When it's a mutual yes, we make the intro.
This one's built for solo founders looking for a co-founder, operators with the itch to build something, exited founders getting back in the game, and grad students who are ready to jump in.
We've run this format 9 times with our members, with a 45% second meeting conversion rate. This is the first time we're opening it up beyond the C2FM community, and we're really excited to bring it to the wider NYC climate and biodiversity ecosystem right before Climate Week.
We're hosting this one with our friends at Ambition Capital, Collide Capital, Comma Capital, Powerhouse Ventures, Precursor, and Superorganism, in partnership with Anywhere Ventures, Goodwin, and Rho!

title: The Energy Transition Deferred: Dr. Jesse Jenkins On The Race For More Power (In-Person)
description:
The AI buildout has a bottleneck, and it isn't chips. It's power. Interconnection queues stretch for years, deals get signed under NDAs, and roughly 70% of Americans now oppose data centers in their own communities, with opposition crossing party lines. The energy transition everyone was promised keeps getting deferred by the race to feed the models.
Yet new Princeton research points to an escape hatch. A 500-megawatt data center able to flex its grid demand for less than 1% of the year can reach full operation three to five years sooner than one that can’t. Jesse Jenkins floated exactly that idea on Season One of Deep Tech LIVE, 18 months ago, when almost nobody was building that way. So is the real bottleneck electrons, or is it contracts and consent?
Dr. Jesse Jenkins leads Princeton's ZERO Lab and the REPEAT Project, and was profiled by the Wall Street Journal as ‘The Professor Helping Guide Billions in Climate Spending.’ He has since added another hat, co-founding Firma Power, where he serves as CTO, working on the challenge of supplying clean firm power to hyperscale data centers.
Jesse and moderator Duncan Turner (General Partner & Managing Director at SOSV HAX) will dig into what the analyst sees now that he is the one selling the power:
Why flexibility, not new generation, may be the fastest path to powering AI
Which new energy technologies are actually helping — from grid hardware and storage to geothermal and nuclear
The exploding opposition to data centers crossing party lines sending midterm candidates scrambling (is it NIMBYism, or something else?)
How “clean firm power” can be delivered to the right places at the right prices and, potentially, make hyperscalers and communities happy
Seats are limited. Register early to save your spot!
This is an in-person event. Location will be shared after you register and are approved.
📍 Broadcast live from our SOSV NY event space, this is the next installment of SOSV Deep Tech LIVE, our video podcast series exploring the frontiers of deep tech with leading founders, researchers, and technologists.

⚡ Public Grid - Platform to lower tenant energy bills & supply energy via energy brokering, community solar, and VPP programs

title: Are targets the wrong starting point?
description:
Roundtable on the future of corporate climate action
Are targets the wrong starting point?
Corporate climate action has been built around top-down targets. These create discipline, but may also push companies to prioritize what counts over what matters.
A contrasting approach starts with capabilities, but tests them against the transition we are trying to build. Companies identify what they can actually change, where they have leverage, and where they can play a meaningful role. That role must be understood in relation to system transformation, not only what shows up neatly in the company’s GHG inventory
Would this unlock greater ambition, or become a free-for-all where every company defines its own convenient version of climate leadership? This session asks how corporate climate strategy can move beyond cookie-cutter targets without losing accountability.
An invitation-only roundtable discussion, starting with brief remarks by Robert Höglund, Head of Climate at Milkywire, and Lisa Sachs, Director of the Columbia Center on Sustainable Investment, followed by a moderated discussion under Chatham House Rule.
Participants will include corporate climate leaders, standards experts, funders, advisors and practitioners working on the next generation of corporate climate strategy.
8:30 - 9:00: Light breakfast and mingle
9:00 - 10:30: Opening remarks and discussionInvite only. Corporate climate practitioners can request an invite by registering.
More information
Milkywire is working on the next generation of corporate climate strategy through published thought leadership and advisory work with leading global companies. The focus is how companies can identify and act on their highest-value climate role, with strategies grounded in action and real-world impact, not only inventory accounting.
Milkywire’s latest publication, Build the world your net zero target assumes, written by Robert Höglund together with Claire Wigg at Exponential Roadmap Initiative, explores this broader shift from “what counts” to “what matters” in corporate climate action.
Moderator: Robert Höglund is head of climate at Milkywire, where he leads work on corporate climate strategy, climate finance and carbon removal. He is a member of the SBTi Expert Working Group and the EU Expert Group on Carbon Removals, co-founder of CDR.fyi, and a frequent writer on corporate climate action and carbon removal.Featured speaker: Lisa Sachs is Director of the Columbia Center on Sustainable Investment and Associate Professor of Professional Practice at Columbia Climate School, where she also directs the M.S. in Climate Finance. Her recent work argues that corporate climate action primarily needs to be assessed by its contribution to systems transformation.

title: Climate Week, but on a Boat
description:
Come ride a boat.
Climate Week has rooftop receptions, invite-only dinners, and panels with the word "nexus" in the title. This is not that. This is the Staten Island Ferry: free, runs 24/7, sails directly past the Statue of Liberty, and is quietly the best harbor cruise in the city. We take the 2:00 boat, look at the skyline, get off at Staten Island, immediately get back on (this is the intermission), and ride home. Back on land by 3:15, in time for whatever evening reception you're pretending you might skip.
Who's this for? Founders, investors, operators, students, policy people, and anyone who's hit their panel limit by Thursday. There's no programming and no moderator. Just an hour of open conversation with the people building and funding climate in NYC, while the Statue of Liberty eavesdrops.
Details:
Meet 1:40 sharp at Whitehall Terminal. The boat leaves at 2:00 whether we're on it or not.
The ferry is free. Do not buy a ticket from anyone. Anyone selling you a ticket is selling you a crime.
We'll be on the right side heading out. That's the Statue side.
If it rains, the boat has an inside. We ride regardless.
RSVP so the morning-of note reaches you and I know who to look for.
